queries: LLM self-correction survey when can LLMs correct their own mistakes
Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet

sources_considered.why: A critical survey of LLM self-correction, revised December 2024 and published in TACL 2024.
OpenAI's SimpleQA paper (November 2024) measures whether models know when they are wrong.
A key study on intrinsic self-correction. It dates from 2023, outside the target period, so it is context only.

receipt.public_excerpt: (1) no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except for studies in tasks that are exceptionally suited for self-correction

evidence_items.explanation: The peer-reviewed survey finds no evidence that prompted LLMs can check and fix their own outputs, except on unusually suitable tasks.
Frontier models, including o1-preview, were reliably overconfident about factual answers. That points to weak self-checking.

receipt.public_excerpt: (2) self-correction works well in tasks that can use reliable external feedback, and (3) large-scale fine-tuning enables self-correction.

evidence_items.explanation: The same survey finds that self-correction works with reliable outside feedback or large-scale fine-tuning. That cuts against an absolute 'inability'.

receipt.public_excerpt: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.

evidence_items.explanation: Earlier evidence for the same pattern. It falls outside the target period, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: There is no single benchmark from the period measuring 'basic' fact checking by the newest reasoning models (o1, o3) without tools.
Search-enabled assistants could check facts through outside tools. Whether that counts is a matter of reading.
